headline: Uncertainty and neighbor fusion address failure modes in molecular property models
label: Molecular Property Prediction Models
summary: Scaffold splits understate out-of-distribution error in ADMET models, prompting label-free structural-frontier evaluation and uncertainty-aware architectures.
synthesis: The dominant thread is uncertainty-aware modeling of molecular properties, in which predictors estimate their own reliability and are assessed under harder evaluation splits. PG-EVIKAL fuses neighbor information at test time using evidential networks and a learned property-distance metric, reducing RMSE on 14 of 16 molecular datasets. AUINet applies Monte Carlo dropout over a D-MPNN to estimate atom-level uncertainty and iteratively refine it toward critical failure structures, while BCATNet fuses classification knowledge into Bayesian transformer regression for bioactivity prediction with uncertainty estimates. On the evaluation side, a label-free structural-frontier split shows that scaffold splits understate out-of-distribution error in ADMET models, and robust penalties (MV-FREX) are evaluated against it. The genomic entries, Evo 2 probes for biosecurity features and weight locking on Evo-1-8k, are adjacent foundation-model work and do not share this molecular-property focus.
